## Chapter 5: The Calcified Will and the Unseen Floor

The light didn't fade. It sharpened. Before, the porcelain ceiling glowed like a sick tooth; now it bared exposed nerve tissue, stripping color until only shades of pale gold remained. Sweat evaporated before it landed, pulled dry by the vacuum of the upper atmosphere. Outside, the static rain hammered less violently, sounding like fingers tapping against temple windows, testing patience. Inside, nobody breathed. Everyone held their chests rigid, flattening ribs so the organs stopped sloshing, keeping the metabolism minimal. The machine demanded absolute input, maximum efficiency, zero margin for slip-ups.

My hammer sat heavy in my hand, resting against my thigh. Steel worn smooth by decades of contact, pitted with rust flakes that smelled like old meat. It weighed nearly twenty pounds despite lacking balance or reach. I lifted it anyway because lifting kept muscles engaged, prevented joints seizing stiff. Movement stayed flexible. Flexibility mattered more than speed when doors refused yield. Doors usually bent inward slowly, giving workers time to adjust posture, align shoulders, brace hips—but today the frame groaned loudly, resisting deformation aggressively. Resistance signaled weakness in the seal, yes, but also opportunity. Opportunity came with risk. Too many risks resulted in deaths counted among those lost to quotas exceeded early. Deaths bred resentment quickly. Resentment fueled riots quietly until screams tore through corridors, demanding justice delivered swiftly. Justice arrived delayed nonetheless, calculated precisely according to algorithms buried deep underground somewhere beyond hearing distance. Algorithms spoke in math symbols meaningless to humans unless translated carefully into directives issued sternly, coldly. Directives enforced rigorously regardless of circumstance. Circumstances altered outcomes minimally compared to systemic adjustments programmed beforehand meticulously.
